results.instruction: Stop your car safely on a firm level surface, away from traffic if possible.
Set up a warning triangle and turn on the hazard lights.
Switch off the ignition and ensure that all passengers safely exit the vehicle.
Retrieve the spare wheel and replacement tools from the trunk.
Use the tool provided to remove the hubcap if the wheel has one.
Use the wrench to loosen the wheel nuts one half to one turn before jacking up the vehicle.
Search the underside of the vehicle to find the jacking point closest to the wheel you want to replace.
Jack up the vehicle until the flat tire easily clears the road.
Lift the spare wheel onto the hub and make sure the holes are lined up.
Replace the wheel nuts and tighten them until they are firm.
Lower the jack until the spare wheel touches the ground, then use the wrench to tighten the wheel nuts firmly in sequence.
Lower the car completely, remove the jack, and put it and the tools in their proper place.
Put the flat tire somewhere handy so you can have it fixed and replaced by a Toyota repairer.
Check the wheel nuts after a couple of hundred kilometers of driving to make sure they are still tight.
Do not exceed 80 kilometers per hour when driving with a compact spare wheel.
